body: Decomposition of 27 Indian winner windows (25 case records plus BEL and both shipyards; screener TTM P/E, split-adjusted prices): log(price multiple) = log(EPS multiple) + log(P/E multiple). Median share of the log-return from rerating = 37%. Long runs (9+ years: Bajaj Finance, Page, Astral, Pidilite, Titan, Eicher, Balkrishna, APL Apollo, Deepak, Tata Elxsi, Garware, Alkyl) had a median rerating share of ~36%; EPS compounding did most of the work. Short runs (≤5.5 years: KPIT 62%, Cochin 88%, HAL 66%, Mazagon 53%, CDSL 50%, Dixon 42%, Kaynes 29%, Trent 14%) had a median of ~51%. Rerating-heavy cases (>50% from P/E: Cochin, HAL, KPIT, Symphony, Balkrishna, Tata Elxsi, Mazagon, CDSL) are a median ~54% below their ATH on 19 Nov 2026. HAL (−14%), whose EPS kept rising, is the exception. Earnings-heavy cases (≤30%: Trent, Page, Titan, Avanti, Eicher, Caplin, La Opala, Polycab, Kaynes) had mixed outcomes: Titan and Eicher are near highs, while La Opala and Kaynes are down 60%+. Where they fell, it was because growth slowed, not because a pure multiple was undone. Rule: when more than half of a gain is multiple, the gain is fragile; check whether EPS can carry the price if P/E returns to its median. Caveat: windows start at lows, which inflates P/E expansion.
title: India multibaggers: ~2/3 of return is EPS, ~1/3 rerating (long runs); ~1/2 rerating (short runs)
